item.title: Bridging digitalisation, sustainability, and resilience through systems thinking tools: Integrated perspectives and collaborative practices for SMEs
item.content:encoded:
Rui Torres de Oliveira, Deakin University

Agnes Toth-Peter, University of Queensland

Martie-Louise Verreynne, University of Queensland

David Audretsch, Indiana University

Domenico Dentoni, MBS School of Business

Andrea Chiarini, University of Verona

The 21st century presents a range of complex and interdependent challenges, including climate change, resource depletion, economic inequality, and technological disruptions. These so-called wicked problems demand a paradigm shift in our approach to problem-solving. Addressing such challenges requires multi-stakeholder partnerships and holistic, systems-level approaches that transcend traditional, siloed methodologies. Systems thinking, a powerful tool for understanding complexity and interconnections, offers a pathway to sustainable solutions.

Appel publié par Journal of Small Business Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Applications of systems thinking tools, such as causal loop diagrams (CLDs), system archetypes, and system dynamics modeling, in addressing sustainability challenges
  • Development and validation of systems-level frameworks and methodologies for sustainable development
  • Case studies demonstrating the impact of systems thinking on real-world sustainability and/or digitalisation initiatives
  • Use of group model building and participatory system dynamics to support interdisciplinary and ecosystem solutions
  • Exploration of system archetypes and system dynamics models to identify leverage points for driving transformational change and to investigate levers in cross-boundary settings
  • The role of digital technologies, including IoT, AI, big data, and blockchain, in enabling systems-level insights and solutions in the circular economy and sustainability initiatives
  • Integration of digitalisation with circular economy strategies and Industry 5.0 principles and potentials
  • Innovative approaches to digital transformation that promote sustainable development
  • Cross-sectoral and interdisciplinary research to foster collaboration in bridging sustainability and digitalisation, using systems thinking
  • The role of ecosystems in sustainable business models and the boundaries of entrepreneurial ecosystems
  • Methodologies for recognising, assessing and addressing the interconnectedness of environmental, economic, and social systems
  • Open innovation in new sustainable businesses, considering distinct institutional contexts and economic systems, such as emerging and developed economies

Timeline

  • October 1, 2026: Rolling submissions begin
  • May 31, 2027: Manuscript deadline for rolling submissions

item.title: Reimagining Small Business Futures - AI, Inclusion, and Territorial Innovation
item.content:encoded:
Nicola Cucari, Sapienza University of Rome

Guanglei Zhang, Wuhan University of Technology

Jintao Lu, Shanxi University of Electronic Science and Technology

Hua Fan, Shanghai International Studies University

Eric Liguori, Florida State University

The global innovation landscape is undergoing a profound restructuring. Collaboration among geographically distributed innovation ecosystems is intensifying. At the same time, the rapid advancement and diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) are reshaping the dynamics of global industrial competition. New innovation hubs are emerging across the Asia-Pacific region, Europe, and several emerging economies. In parallel, digital technologies, platformization, and the decentralization of computing power are reducing traditional geographical and scale barriers. As a result, the conditions for competition and innovation are being fundamentally redefined. In this context, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are no longer structurally disadvantaged. Instead, they can increasingly act as agile and innovation-driven players within global value chains.

Appel publié par Journal of Small Business Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • AI-driven business model innovation in SMEs
  • Digital transformation pathways under technological turbulence
  • AI and sustainable competitive advantage in resource-constrained firms
  • AI-enabled work redesign and organizational reconfiguration in SMEs
  • Inclusive AI ecosystems for minority, women, migrant, and informal entrepreneurs
  • Algorithmic Bias and transparency in AI-assisted SMEs
  • AI-enabled territorial innovation and smart regional development
  • Public policies supporting equitable AI adoption among SMEs
  • AI, cybersecurity, and risk governance in small businesses
  • Human–AI collaboration and entrepreneurial decision-making
  • Data strategies and knowledge management in SMEs
  • Data ownership and territorial digital autonomy in AI-driven SME development
  • Ethical, social, and governance implications of AI adoption
  • AI platforms and SME participation in digital value chains
  • AI for local resilience, crisis response, and adaptive entrepreneurship

item.title: Novel Forms and Models of Organization
item.content:encoded:
Masatoshi Kato, Kwansei Gakuin University

David Audretsch, Indiana University

Roy Thurik, Erasmus University Rotterdam

Maksim Belitski, University of Reading

Alex Coad, Waseda Business School

Eric Liguori, Florida State University

Rapid technological change, globalization of supply chains and demand, increasing physical and digital connectivity, and inter-dependencies between actors in innovation and entrepreneurial ecosystems are forcing entrepreneurs and managers to rethink how they organize beyond the manufacturing of products and services, how they innovate, what technologies they adopt, and what markets they enter. The forms and models of organization affect a firm's ability to become exceptional. At the core of firm organization, the factors that distinguish them from their counterparts in the industry and region are firm size, firm age, stage of entrepreneurial continuum, institutional context, and technology-savviness. Firms that have been able to optimize their organization will outperform their regional competitors, markets, and industry; create new forms of growth at a different pace; and approach the innovation and production frontier. Through organizations in different forms, entrepreneurs and mature firms create product and process innovation and coordinate people, external ecosystem actors, government, suppliers, and capital to achieve frontier outcomes.

Appel publié par Journal of Small Business Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How do firms adopting novel forms of organization differ in leadership, governance, and decision-making, and how do these differences shape innovation and productivity at the frontier?
  • What internal microstructures (e.g., boards, design, cross-functional teams, routines) enable firms to combine and recombine internal capabilities with external knowledge and ecosystem actors to achieve exceptional performance?
  • How do novel organizational forms affect authority, accountability, and coordination across functions, and what are the effects on innovation speed, product and managerial innovation, value creation, talent retention, growth, and scaling?
  • Which combinations of internal investment (make), external acquisition (buy), and alliance orchestration (ally) constitute novel organizational models that sustain frontier performance across firm types (hidden champions, niche leaders, sustained innovators, blitzscalers, scalers, etc.)?
  • How does the diversity (institutional and geographic) of external knowledge and innovation partners translate into firms adopting novel forms of organization, and what internal routines convert diverse inputs into outcomes?
  • Under what conditions do international vs regional knowledge collaboration and spillovers generate non-redundant knowledge that improves innovation and performance, and how do firms with different organizational forms apply, filter, and integrate this knowledge?
  • How does digitalization (AI and robotics, data systems, cloud, prominent role of intangibles, etc.) reshape internal process architectures, and which organizational forms best convert digital investments into productivity and innovation gains?
  • Which governance models (data rights, intellectual property, cybersecurity, partner contracts) enable novel organizational forms to adopt and scale complex technologies while maintaining trust and control in technology and partners?
  • How do digitally savvy firms pivot and reconfigure organizational forms to build resilience to supply, demand, and geopolitical shocks, and what design features predict faster recovery and sustained innovation?
  • How do firms implement novel forms of organization while embedded in industry and entrepreneurial ecosystems, and how does ecosystem position shape organizational models for innovation and scaling?
  • How do niche leaders and other exceptional performers orchestrate global supply chains as an organizational capability, not only a sourcing choice, across regional and international contexts?
  • What partner portfolio mixes (universities, suppliers, customers, competitors, government, research labs, conferences, competitions, trade and industrial associations, scientific communities) are associated with frontier outcomes, and what form of organization do firms need to adopt to efficiently govern such collaborations, knowledge spillovers, and firm strategies?
  • How do relationships with government shape novel organizational models through procurement, standards, subsidies, and cluster governance, and when do these relationships enhance versus constrain innovation and productivity?
  • How do organizational models vary between emerging and traditional industries and across industrial clusters of novel and emerging industries where traditional forms of organization are no longer working?
  • How do deglobalization pressures and techno-nationalism reshape firms' organizational choices?
  • What distinctive business model configurations characterize exceptional performers across countries, regions, industries, and stages of growth, age, and size, and how are these configurations enabled by organizational form?
  • How do European, Asian, American, and African leaders in WEIRD and non-WEIRD countries differ in adopting and experimenting with novel forms of organization?
  • What contextual factors explain these cross-country differences?
  • Do niche leaders exhibit distinctive innovation patterns (radical vs incremental, product vs process, ecosystem vs standalone), and which organizational designs best explain variation in these patterns and their performance effects?

Timeline

  • November 1, 2026: Manuscript submission opens
  • November 15, 2026: Submission deadline for extended abstracts and full papers
  • January 31, 2027: Manuscript deadline

item.title: Reform to Renewal: Succession, Socioemotional Wealth, and the Future of Chinese Family Businesses
item.content:encoded:
James Vardaman, University of Memphis

Feigu Zhou, University of Montevallo

Eric Liguori, Florida State University

Shuai Jin, Jiangsu University

Weiwen Li, Sun Yat-sen University

The Theories of Family Enterprise Conference is pleased to partner with Jiangsu University to host a special TOFE research colloquium focused on the future of Chinese family businesses (TOFE China). Submissions will be considered for fast-track review and publication in a forthcoming Journal of Small Business Management (JSBM) special collection. This collection is affiliated with a colloquium scheduled for January 9th, 2027, at Jiangsu University in Zhenjiang, Jiangsu Province, China. Scholars from around the world are invited to submit to the colloquium, with a special invitation to scholars who inhabit the Chinese context. The colloquium provides an opportunity for authors to receive developmental feedback directly from JSBM editors and a pathway to publication in the special collection, subject to JSBM's standard peer review process.

Appel publié par Journal of Small Business Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Founder succession and leadership transfer in post-reform family firms
  • Successor identity formation and legitimacy
  • Preservation versus erosion of SEW during succession
  • Tensions between family control and professionalization
  • Emotional attachment, family identity, and transgenerational intentions
  • SEW and strategic renewal
  • Long-term consequences of Reform and Opening for family enterprise
  • State–family business relationships over time
  • Family and nonfamily employee experiences
  • Shared identity and organizational identification
